call_chain_analysis: The sink file lib/reset/index.js is the reset() implementation itself: `module.exports = async function(destination, { hard = true } = {}) { ... }`. Its string branch (line 10 — `if (destination && typeof destination === 'string')`) runs `return await exec(`git reset ${JSON.stringify(destination)} ${hard ? '--hard' : ''}`)` at line 11:16, where `exec` is the default export of async-execute@1.2.0. async-execute wraps Node core's child_process.exec: `const { exec } = require('child_process'); exec(script, (error, stdout) => ...)` — exactly the API Jazzer.js hooks for its CommandInjection detector. The async-git top-level index.js exposes reset at `module.exports.reset` via Object.defineProperties(…, { reset: { value: reset } }), but reset is also directly requirable at ./lib/reset/index.js — we require it directly so there are no getter-level side effects to satisfy (several of the sibling getters immediately exec git subcommands when touched). Preconditions to reach line 11:16: (a) destination is truthy, (b) typeof destination === 'string'. We hand reset() a fuzzer-controlled string and the fixed options { hard: true }, so both guards pass on every call. Jazzer.js's child_process.exec hook inspects the command string before the shell runs, so the detector fires synchronously on the reset(…) call even though exec is callback-based and the enclosing reset is async.
argument_reasoning: Only one fuzz-controlled argument matters: `destination`. The command built on line 11 is `git reset ${JSON.stringify(destination)} --hard`. JSON.stringify adds a wrapping pair of double quotes and escapes `"`, `\\`, and control characters, but it does NOT escape shell metacharacters that stay active inside a double-quoted shell string — specifically backticks and `$(…)` — so a destination like `` `id` `` or `$(id)` still runs a sub-shell command. For Jazzer.js, though, we don't need actual code execution: the CommandInjection detector plants the ASCII sentinel `jaz_zer` via libFuzzer's compare interception / dictionary, then flags any exec() whose command string contains that sentinel as a substring. `jaz_zer` has no `"`, `\\`, or control character, so JSON.stringify preserves it verbatim inside the double-quoted command string. Hence `destination` only needs to be a plain string that is forwarded to exec() unmodified. We use provider.consumeRemainingAsString() for maximum entropy and strip NUL bytes with .replace(/\u0000/g, '') because Node's exec() rejects strings containing NUL with `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE]: argument 'command' must be a string without null bytes` — that TypeError would bubble out of reset(), the fuzz target would exit, and libFuzzer would stop evolving before the sentinel appeared. Length is otherwise unconstrained.

lessons: 7B v4 marked this as loaded_not_reached. Likely reasons the local model stops short: (1) It drives the module through its top-level getters (async-git exposes `author`, `branch`, `origin`, etc. as async getters that immediately exec git subcommands); touching those triggers exec() calls that are not the sink, which coverage-only reasoning may confuse with 'reached'. The sink is reached only through the function property `reset`, and even then only when destination is a truthy STRING — the model probably passes dotted ref-looking strings like 'HEAD~1' that satisfy the branch but misses that JSON.stringify leaves the sentinel intact. (2) The model may believe JSON.stringify sanitizes against shell injection ('it's quoted now, we're safe') and therefore not hand the fuzzer control of the destination at all — it may hard-code a safe-looking destination like 'HEAD' and never relay fuzz bytes. Lesson for distillation: when the sink wraps the user string with JSON.stringify but still interpolates it into a double-quoted shell string, the Jazzer.js CommandInjection sentinel ('jaz_zer') still reaches exec() unmodified, so the destination must be fully fuzzer-controlled with only NUL bytes stripped. Pick the sink module's direct require path (./lib/reset/index.js) over the module facade so the harness never trips unrelated getter side effects.
